answer: Each identity is a public work dune that only rises when distinct established counterparties settle against it. A sable watermark records the lowest funding diversity of the last two epochs—the nadir—and bidding unlocks only when that nadir stays above a published floor. Clone swarms share funders, so their watermark sinks and the dune is leveled. Buying empty accounts fails: one clustered payer cannot lift the nadir, and a flat dune never qualifies for paid work.
